picks.style: sanskrit invocation, tanpura drone and bamboo flute, deep male voice, slow, questioning
picks.why: The question that starts the whole epic — 'Who in this world today is truly virtuous?' — a litany of questions that stands alone.

picks.style: soaring sanskrit chant, tanpura and rapid tabla, bright male voice, fast, exhilarated
picks.why: Hanumān flying the moon's path, bursting in and out of cloud-banks, with Siṃhikā waiting below.

picks.style: sanskrit lament, sarangi and low drone, grieving male voice, slow, heavy
picks.why: Rāvaṇa over Indrajit, each line beginning 'Today' and ending 'where have you gone, abandoning us all?'

picks.style: roman comic aria, double pipes and hand drum, exasperated male voice, brisk, mock-heroic
picks.why: The penniless lover claiming his labours outdo Hercules' — lion, Hydra, stag, boar, birds of Stymphalus.

picks.style: patter song, plucked lyre and clappers, fast male voice, rattling, boastful
picks.why: The parasite's ancestral trade recited down the generations: 'just like mice, always fed on the victuals of others.'

picks.style: roman banquet duet, tibiae and tambourine, two warm voices, lilting, amorous
picks.why: 'Why am I without you? And why are you without me?' — a love duet that walks straight to the couches.

picks.style: baroque dramatic aria, harpsichord and strings, steady soprano, measured, unflinching
picks.why: Arria stabs herself first and hands back the dagger smiling: 'O Petus, thus, thy Fate command.'

picks.style: visionary art song, chamber organ and viol, clear high voice, slow, rising
picks.why: The soul climbing away from earth — 'Yonder's the little Ball of Earth, it lessens as I rise.'

picks.style: pindaric sea ode, cello and harpsichord, warm alto, swelling, restless
picks.why: A whole storm-at-sea figure for a life of business, ending in the plea for a safe retreat.

picks.style: village lament ballad, solo fiddle and guitar, aged male voice, slow, rueful
picks.why: The old athlete counting what his arm could once lift, now 'wither'd, weak' — plain quatrains, real grief.

picks.style: skeptic's air, spare piano and cello, dry baritone, unhurried, wry
picks.why: 'Our joys are false, and false our tears' — and the rainbow that vanishes when you reach it.

picks.style: georgian elegy, string quartet, plaintive tenor, slow, formal
picks.why: A clean elegy opening: 'His Wisdom Folly, Length of Time a Span, his Life is Vanity, his Death is Woe.'

picks.style: greek symposium song, lyre and soft aulos, conversational tenor, easy, reflective
picks.why: A run of pungent quoted verses on old age, buried grief, and the sweetness of remembering past toils.

picks.style: banquet air, kithara and hand drum, light male voice, gentle, abundant
picks.why: Ends on the orchard line — 'The fig-trees sweet, the apple-trees that bear fair fruit, and olives green through all the year.'

picks.style: sublime greek hymn, deep drone and struck strings, resonant male voice, vast, surging
picks.why: Poseidon striding, the sea-beasts gambolling from their lairs, the sea parting for joy — then Sappho's 'he seems to me equal to the gods'.

picks.style: storm ode, low strings and rolling percussion, urgent voice, driving, fearful
picks.why: The Homeric wave burying the ship in foam, the sailors borne a little way out of reach of death.

picks.style: greek dance song, aulos and finger cymbals, light voices, quick, circling
picks.why: Only candidate; a chain of lines about dancing, with 'their dainty feet round the dark waters dance, about the altar of Zeus.'

picks.style: sea-trader's chant, bowed lyre and low drum, rough male voice, steady, working
picks.why: Only candidate; three lines of barter at a harbour — copper, steel, hides, cattle, slaves — concrete and chantable.
